constraint_decided_it: E14's scope note limits it to 'assessing the state of preservation of an object during a particular period', and P35 has identified: E14 -> E3, whose scope note limits E3 to 'the prevailing physical condition of any material object or feature during a specific instance of E52 Time-Span'. A prospective fitness-for-purpose verdict inferred from a measured rate is neither a state of preservation nor a physical condition holding over an asserted time-span, so B's E14/P35/E3 'fit for sea service' construct falls outside both scope notes. Both answers are within domain/range on the E16 half (P39 E16->E18, P40 E16->E54, P16 E7->E70).

Certificate's fitness declaration = a separate downstream act: E17 Type Assignment (P41 classified the chronometer, P42 assigned an E55 Type 'fit for sea service') or, following Issue 482's preferred route, a CRMinf/CRMsci inference-making class (I5/S5, J2 concluded that); the certificate itself is an E31 Document that P70 documents both. Neither answer names P41/P42 or the E31 certificate.
reasoning: Both answers reach the same, correct answer to the question as asked -- the eleven-day trial is E16 Measurement of an E54 Dimension, not E14 -- and every property either proposes respects its declared domain and range, so they separate only on the certificate's 'fit for sea service' clause. A routes it to E17 or a CRMinf inference-making class and supports this from Issue 482, which asks verbatim whether 'Exposure Assessment' IsA E17 Type Assignment or S8 Categorical Hypothesis Making and prefers I5/S5 Inference Making -- E14 is not among the SIG's candidates for a judgement derived from measurements. B instead puts the verdict in E14 -> P35 -> E3 typed 'fit for sea service', which its own quotation of E14's scope note ('assessing the state of preservation') defeats, and it rejects E17 on the false ground that the class is taxonomic, when E17's scope note reads 'classifying items of whatever kind ... where the value of the classification depends on the personal opinion of the classifier' -- exactly a certifier's dated verdict. B's other citations are sound: t1631 does contain Doerr's 'Data Evaluation' distinction and his 'direct comparative measurements ... putting two figurines side by side', and t1406/t1781 do carry the Sinai Greek 418 P34/P35/E3 'fine'/'broken' pattern, but that pattern is about preservation, which is precisely why it does not transfer to a performance verdict.
